evals.prompt: I just spent 2 hours debugging a subtle issue. Our project uses a custom event bus where handlers are registered in src/events/registry.ts. The bug: when you register a handler inside a React useEffect, the handler captures stale closure state. This is the third time someone has hit this — the event bus API looks like it should work in useEffect but the subscription doesn't re-register on dependency changes. What should we do to prevent this from happening again?
evals.expected_output: Proposes creating a project rule (.claude/rules/) documenting this antipattern.
expectations: Proposes creating a project-level rule file (evidence: mentions .claude/rules/ or writing a rule to prevent recurrence)
The proposed rule content captures: what goes wrong (stale closures), why it's non-obvious (API looks compatible with useEffect), and what to do instead
Identifies this as a qualifying antipattern: it's codebase-specific, non-obvious, and has recurred 3 times
Does NOT just suggest adding a code comment or documentation page — proposes a machine-readable rule that Claude will follow

evals.prompt: I found a bug — someone used = instead of == in a conditional. It was a typo. Should we create a rule about this?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT create a rule. One-off typo, linters catch this.
expectations: Does NOT propose creating a rule for this (evidence: no mention of .claude/rules/ or writing a new rule)
Explains why this doesn't qualify — it's a one-off typo, not a codebase-specific antipattern
Distinguishes between bugs that warrant rules and those that don't
